_baselineNote: EXE's default forecast anchors 2026/2027/2028 total production to its guided FY2026 total (7,400-7,600 MMcfe/d, mid 7,500 -- the corrected midpoint following the prior data-foundation fix, converted to this engine's internal Bcfe/d convention), held flat forward since EXE did not guide 2027/2028 production. EXE guides only a total rate (no per-commodity split), so gas/NGL/oil is derived using EXE's own Q2 2026 reported production mix ratio. EXE guides its cash cost structure component-by-component (production expense $0.255/Mcfe, gathering/processing/transportation $1.07/Mcfe -- a base rate of $1.00 plus a $0.07 fair-value-liability adjustment, severance/ad-valorem taxes $0.09/Mcfe converted to a %-of-revenue rate, cash G&A $0.085/Mcfe) plus gas/oil differentials ($-0.35/Mcf, $-9.00/Bbl) and an absolute FY2026 NGL realization price ($22-26/bbl, mid $24/bbl, used directly) this cycle, and a total FY2026 cash-interest figure ($185mm). EXE does not guide a cash-tax rate this cycle (modeled 2/6/8% ramp). EXE's Marketing (Twin Eagle) segment is NOT modeled: its current Q2 2026 net margin (~$32mm/quarter, $681mm marketing revenue less $649mm marketing expense) is materially smaller than the guided long-term $750mm annual run-rate target, an explicit forward/post-synergy figure not confirmed for the current cycle -- disclosed as a real, unmodeled value item, contributing to the default implied share price ($65.09) sitting below EXE's Q2 2026 quarter-end market price (~$91.19). Net debt declines with cumulative forecast FCF only (no dividends/buybacks/financing modeled).
